main_text.p: apparet, Saracenos dici non à Sara, Abrahamí vxore, quod est ridiculum. Hoc enim modo oporteret aut à Sara Saraos dictos, aut uxorem Abrahami non Saram, sed Saratam vocatam fuisse. Avellenda est haec opinio de animis hominum. Arabes porró dicti sunt ab Hebraica voce herāb, vespera, quæ dicitur à miscendo, seu commiscendo, quia tunc lux tenebris miscetur: tropicè est mixtura variorum populorum, turba miscellanea, &c. Ier. 25,20,24. Vbi Kimchi scribit Arabes vagos & mixtos, Habitantes tabernacula intelligi, qui ob id Plinio dicti Scenitæ pastionibus inprimis vacabant. Vnde νομάδες dicti ἀπὸ τῆς νέμειν, à pascendo. Depastis enim herbis uno in loco pastiliones suos curribus alio transvehunt. quod præter alios Esaias innuit cap. 13 v. 20. Neque figet tentorium ibi Arabs: scilicet ad pecus suum ibi pascendum. quod signum erat inter alia excidii Babylonici, quod Propheta prædicit. Sive autem Hagarenos & Saracenos, sive Arabes dixeris uno nomine, lingua usi sunt, hodieque utuntur, eâ, quæ præter Hebræam & Chaldæam, omnibus cæteris drior, & antiquior est, & quasi mater earum censetur, in Africa Asiaq; ita vigens, ut eam

page.notes: Greek word in the paragraph "Vnde" is transcribed approximately: νομάδες and ἀπὸ τῆς νέμειν are uncertain [?]. Hebrew words "herāb" and "vespera" printed in Hebrew-script with Latin transliteration in print; the Hebrew characters are not reliably legible from the scan. The last line is partly obscured by a dark stain at the bottom left and is uncertain. Several words in the text are blurred and not certain; the page is in a worn state. Running head reads COMMENTARIUS with a stop-like mark after it, printed as "COMMENTARIUS." and the page number 94 at top right.
